abstract: The Hobart–Brouwer table of directed strongly regular graph parameters lists the complementary pair $(96,46,32,24,20)$ and $(96,49,35,22,28)$ as unresolved. We construct a dsrg$(96,46,32,24,20)$, so both parameter sets exist. The graph is a Cayley digraph on the group $K$ of affine maps $x\mapsto ux+b$ of the Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(4,2)=\mathbb Z_4[w]/(w^2+w+1)$, where $u$ runs over a cyclic unit group of order 6; $K$ is SmallGroup(96,71). We list the connection set $S$ explicitly (46 elements). The proof is the identity $(S-6)(S+2)=20K$ in the group ring $\mathbb Z[K]$. Two dependency-free scripts that share no code check it independently, and one of them also builds the $96\times96$ matrices and checks every two-walk count. Computations with nauty and GAP, not used in the proof, show the following. The automorphism group has order 192, is SmallGroup(192,1008), acts with point stabiliser $C_2$ and rank 52, and is imprimitive. The graph is not isomorphic to its converse, so there are at least two non-isomorphic dsrgs with each parameter set. The six cosets of the translation subgroup form an equitable partition with quotient matrix $-2I+8J$, and each coset induces two copies of $K_{2,2,2,2}$. In every nonlinear irreducible representation $\rho$ of $K$ (degrees 3, 3, 6, 6), $\rho(S)=-2I+8P_\rho$ with $P_\rho$ an idempotent of rank one. The graph was found by a sweep of coset actions of groups of order 192 on the cosets of a subgroup of order 2, combining an exact character sieve with CP-SAT models solved separately for each admissible character pattern. The sweep is incomplete. The only published classification at degree 96 that we know of treats primitive groups of rank at most 30, while the automorphism group of our graph is imprimitive of rank 52.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: A focused revision with the two corrections requested in the review of version 1 and one self-found correction. (1) Review point 1: Section 2 now describes [3] correctly. Its Section 4 builds dsrgs from representations of rank at most 30 of GO/SO(4,3) and M11 and obtains six parameter sets at v = 96, none of them ours; its Section 5 classifies the dsrgs admitting a transitive group of degree at most 30, or a primitive group of degree 31-110 and rank at most 30. Neither part can produce our graph, because every group acting transitively on it is imprimitive with at least 52 orbits on ordered pairs. The last sentence of the abstract is corrected in the same way. (2) Review point 2: Appendix A now says that the scalar-block equations were added only for constituents of multiplicity at least 2, and that in the successful pattern no such constituent lies in one eigenspace. (3) Self-found error: the version 1 bullet in Section 2 on our 30 October CP-SAT search over Cayley digraphs of groups of order 96 was wrong (that search was for a different parameter set) and is deleted. (4) Appendix A adds a seed test: the model with the pattern free also finds the graph, in 1 of 3 runs at 300 s and 0 of 5 at 60 s. (5) Section 6 now mentions that the review of version 1 reran both proof scripts. The construction, the proof, the supplement and the hashes are unchanged.
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (96,46,32,24,20) and (96,49,35,22,28)
